analysis:
The PR modifies docs/architecture/inference.md only. The visible patch changes the "Last updated" date, the GLM-5 Next video-handling prose (variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks are now indexed at i / nominalFrameRate instead of refused), and other head-side ranges (head 876-880 and 1717-1726). No code, configuration, key handling, authorization, attestation or cache implementation changes in the supplied evidence.

The supplied units are base-text excerpts, lines 1611-2365 of the base file. The changed ranges at head lines 1717-1726 correspond to a region near the reasoning-parser text (local HTTP responder, `resolveReasoningParser`). The patch excerpt is truncated, so that hunk's content is not visible. I could not verify what it says. It is documentation only, so any security claim in it is unverified.

The base text reviewed in these units covers prefix-cache/SSD, MTP checkpoints, sampling defaults, media caps, MiMo native admission and memory accounting, and tool parsing. It is all unchanged context. It restates existing controls: bounded media ingest, content-free context-exceeded errors, no media-prefix reuse, and encrypted SSD prefix caching. These are consistent with T-041 (SEC-035 accepted risk) and TB-007, and I saw no contradiction with the threat model.

The one security-relevant behavior change implied by the patch is that the GLM-5 Next processor now accepts variable-frame-rate video that it previously refused with a deterministic 400. That is a runtime behavior change if the code matches the doc. The decoded-frame cap (512 MiB) and the 28,532-token cap remain stated, so resource bounds appear preserved. Whether the code enforces the caps for VFR input cannot be verified from this documentation diff, so the integration pass should check the corresponding source change if it is in another batch.

No findings.
